title: Frontier AI Regulation
hook: How do you regulate models too new to have rules yet? This paper sketches three building blocks: set standards, make labs report, then enforce.
key_points: Targets 'frontier AI' — highly capable foundation models that could pose risks to public safety.
Proposes three building blocks: standard-setting, registration and reporting, and compliance and enforcement.
Recommends pre-deployment risk assessments and external scrutiny of models.
Calls for evaluation-gated deployment decisions plus post-deployment monitoring.
content_html: Markus Anderljung, Joslyn Barnhart, Anton Korinek, and co-authors focus on how to govern "frontier AI" — highly capable foundation models whose capabilities could pose risks to public safety. They propose three regulatory building blocks: standard-setting for developers, registration and reporting that give regulators visibility into what is being built, and compliance and enforcement mechanisms to back it up.
extra_html:
How it works

The three building blocks stack into a regime. Standards define what responsible development looks like; registration and reporting let regulators see which frontier models exist and how they behave; compliance and enforcement give the standards teeth. On top of this, the authors recommend concrete safety standards: pre-deployment risk assessments, external scrutiny of models, deployment decisions gated on those evaluations, and continued monitoring after a model is released.

Why it matters

Frontier models advance faster than most legal frameworks can track, and their risks can be hard to anticipate from the outside. By naming specific mechanisms — visibility before harm, evaluation before release, oversight after — the paper offers regulators and labs a shared vocabulary for governing capabilities that don't yet have settled rules.

related.title: Model Evaluation for Extreme Risks
related.hook: General-purpose AI tends to pick up dangerous capabilities alongside useful ones. So test for those capabilities directly — before you ship, not after.

related.title: The EU AI Act
related.hook: The EU's answer to regulating AI: sort systems by how much risk they pose, then scale the rules to match — from outright bans to no rules at all.
